title: Timeframes
hook: Higher timeframes tell the story. Lower timeframes let you step inside it.

launchpad.outcome: Explain what actually changes when you switch chart timeframes, and what doesn't.
launchpad.missionQuestion: If the 1M looks messy and confusing, what should you actually do first?

slides.body:
Every timeframe shows the same market, just zoomed to a different level of detail.

The 4H shows the fewest candles but the clearest big-picture direction. Zoom into 1H, then 15M, and you start seeing the smaller moves inside that bigger picture. By the 1M, you get the most detail, and the most noise. Every tiny wiggle can look urgent there.

slides.title: The 1M looks messy. What now?
slides.body: You open your chart straight to the 1M. It's choppy and confusing, every candle looks like a signal.

options.label: Stay on the 1M and react to what I see
options.feedback: This is how beginners get pulled around by noise, every candle starts to feel urgent.

options.label: Zoom out to the 4H first
options.feedback: Yes. Get the bigger picture before the small candles get to decide your mood.

nodes.prompt: You keep reacting to the 1M. Ten minutes later, you're not even sure if you're bullish or bearish anymore. What now?

options.label: Keep watching the 1M, the answer has to be in here somewhere
options.outcomeText: Still stuck. The bigger picture only lives on the bigger timeframe. No amount of staring at the 1M will produce it.

options.label: Stop, and zoom out to the 4H

nodes.prompt: On the 4H, the bigger picture is actually pretty clear, a clean move in one direction. Now what?

options.label: Go back to the 1M with that context in mind
options.outcomeText: This is the clean flow. The 4H gives you the big picture, then the 1M makes sense INSIDE that picture instead of trying to explain everything by itself.

options.label: Ignore the 4H and go back to just reacting on the 1M
options.outcomeText: Right back where you started. Context doesn't help if you don't carry it with you.

slides.quote: The market doesn't change when you switch the chart view, your perspective does. Always zoom out before you zoom in. Context first, detail second.

slides.prompt: Imagine another AGHF member asks: "Why does it matter which timeframe I look at first?" How would you explain it to them?
slides.modelAnswer: Every timeframe shows the same market, just zoomed to a different level of detail. The 4H shows the big picture with the least noise, so I check that first to know the overall direction. The 1M shows way more detail, but without the 4H's context, every small move on the 1M can feel like a signal when it's really just noise. Checking the bigger timeframe first gives the smaller one a job to do, instead of asking it to explain everything alone.

takeaways: Every timeframe is a different zoom on the same price story.
Higher timeframes show direction; lower timeframes show detail.
Zoom out before you zoom in, context first, detail second.
remember: The market doesn't change when you switch the chart view, your perspective does.
